issue.title: Add DefaultConstraint

labels.name: requires:docs
labels.description: Issues that require documentation be added

milestone.description: The next major version of NUnit.

issue.body:
Sometimes it is needed to verify value type against default value. 
Common use case - verify that value in rest response is not empty, e.g. Guid (not empty) or enums (not Undefined value).

Current alternative - using EqualConstraint (e.g. `Is.Not.EqualTo(Guid.Empty)`, `Is.Not.EqualTo(default(MyEnumTypeName))`), which is not always convenient.

Details:
1. If actual is non-nullable value type - should pass if `actual == default`.

2. If actual is nullable value type - should pass if `actual` is equal to default value of underlying type, so the following code could be possible:
```
MyValueType? actual = ...;
Assert.That(actual, Is.Not.Null & Is.Not.Default);
```

Open question - what the expected behavior if nullable `actual` is null? Technically it is default value for nullable value type, but I think would make sense to fail it in this case, i.e. only account for underlying type default value.

3. Not sure about the behavior for reference types. Not sure it should be allowed at all. Another option - allow (passing when null), and provide roslyn analyzer with warning if used against reference type.

body:
It looks like `Assert.That(default(ICollection), Is.Empty)` throws an `ArgumentException`. _The actual value must be a string, ..._
and `Assert.That(default(ICollection), Is.EquivalentTo(Array.Empty<string()))` throws with mesage _Expected IEnumerable But was: null_

So it looks like in all cases, one would need to check for `null` (or Default) first, so maybe this does not need changing in NUnit.
In my case that would mean inserting an `Assert.That(actualValue.IsDefault, Is.False)` or use the new DefaultConstraint when available.

And maybe we need to add an nunit.analyzer rule warning about passing a possible `null` values to these constraints.

I don't think NUnit should treat `default(ImmutableArray<T>)` as though it was `ImmutableArray<T>.Empty`. This will hide problems in my code.

If we work against the way ImmutableArray was intended to differentiate between `.IsDefault` and `.IsEmpty`, what about a user-defined struct type that implements `IEnumerable<T>` and is also invalid when default?

`Is.Default` sounds good to me.
I'm unsure if there's still interest in this getting fixed, but I noticed that we solved a similar case in the `EqualConstraint` for `ArraySegment` in the past in #477

I haven't checked the scenarios described in https://github.com/nunit/nunit/issues/477#issuecomment-73454620 for `ImmutableArray` but if they _don't hold_ here then I'm wondering if this should be closed given the presence of `Is.Default` and @jnm2 's points above

This type of error is an occupational hazard of using default structs which themselves throw these exceptions when you call through IEnumerable interfaces on them, not unique to NUnit. We could always provide hints added onto assertion messages if we detect a misunderstanding though.

Note that the [`IsEmpty`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Collections.Immutable/src/System/Collections/Immutable/ImmutableArray_1.Minimal.cs#L157) property on `ImmutableArray` will throw a `NullReferenceException`: 
```csharp
get { return this.array!.Length == 0; }
```

There is even a comment on the [`Length`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Collections.Immutable/src/System/Collections/Immutable/ImmutableArray_1.Minimal.cs#L169) property: `We intentionally do not check this.array != null, and throw NullReferenceException if this is called while uninitialized.`
Perhaps Is.EquivalentTo could first check `EqualityComparer<T>.Default.Equals` and return true if that returns true?

I think that's a nice easy win for the happy path here, for all types :)

If we're in agreement on approach here for the equivalent scenario, I'd like to suggest this again as a `good first issue`.

rename.from: IsEquivalent/Is.Not.Empty on default ImmutableArray throws exception.
rename.to: IsEquivalent on default ImmutableArray throws exception.

body:
Hey guys, I'd like to try to work this one out 😊

In order to have `Is.EquivalentTo` to first check `EqualityComparer<T>.Default.Equals` we'd need to add this check at [`CollectionEquivalentConstraint.Matches`](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/af7b9413f9cb7b5780753db6edd1ec7ef0a4ffe1/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Constraints/CollectionEquivalentConstraint.cs#L42) before the Tally initialization right? Which is what fails when trying to apply the [`CollectionTally.ToList`](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/af7b9413f9cb7b5780753db6edd1ec7ef0a4ffe1/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Constraints/CollectionTally.cs#L73) to the uninitialized IEnumerable. Should we try to prevent this method from failing with such argument?

Thanks @mr-sergito ! We'd definitely welcome your contribution here.
That's right :) Effectively we'd be adding a "fast path" here where, if `EqualityComparer<T>.Default.Equals()` returns true would then allow us to skip the relatively more expensive `CollectionTally` operations altogether - which in the process should also then fix the issue when trying to compare equivalency of two `default(ImmutableArray)`s.

So the following [commit](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/commit/70984b0abc13821a55bbc0afc9bfd463cfd4d7b5) would solve the scenarios mentioned [here](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/issues/3772#issuecomment-2325159917). 

However, it'd still fail [here](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/af7b9413f9cb7b5780753db6edd1ec7ef0a4ffe1/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Constraints/CollectionTally.cs#L132) whenever either of the collections is default and the other isn't. 
Should we handle these cases somehow?

My leaning is still to let it crash, since this not an issue specific to NUnit but is just how the ImmutableArray type implements the collection interfaces. You'll see the same issue everywhere, including with LINQ methods.

I'm in favor of that too. I suspect most usages here seek happy path "is equivalent" behavior which this now permits. 
An equivalency test receiving a default + non-default ImmutableArray or a "not equivalent" test with the same data would likely be much rarer and, as @jnm2 points out, also liable to exceptions within parts of the BCL
I also think we shouldn't deal with uninitialized ImmutableArray as it would be hiding potential errors in real scenarios.
